source: GitHub traffic API (14-day window, reporting lags by a day or two)
reading: two page views in the whole window, both on days something was published: nobody is reading the repository
454 clones with 169 distinct cloners but 2 views is not a human pattern; install specs, mirrors and crawlers fetch repositories without opening them
the single referrer is github.com itself, so no external page links to the repository yet

whatThisChanges.previousFraming: the product has installs but no decisions, so retention is the problem
whatThisChanges.measuredFraming: there is no measurable acquisition: the decision count is zero because the arrival count is zero, and a retention metric cannot diagnose an audience that never arrived
whatThisChanges.consequence: F1 (no decisions after a week) would not falsify the product so much as measure an empty funnel; the acquisition question has to be answered first

limitsOfThisEvidence: in-app market installs never touch the repository or its traffic counters, so this measures repository reach, not plugin reach
GitHub counts bot traffic in clones and cannot separate it from people
no analytics exist on the Pages site by design, so site reach is unmeasured rather than zero
